faq.question: What is the best laksa in Singapore?
faq.answer: Janggut Laksa at Roxy Square is consistently ranked #1 by food critics. 928 Yishun Laksa (4.4 stars) and Sungei Road Laksa are close runners-up.

faq.question: How much does laksa cost in Singapore?
faq.answer: Most hawker laksa costs S$3-6 per bowl. The cheapest is 63 Laksa at Ghim Moh from S$2.80. Premium stalls like 328 Katong charge $7.30-$9.30.

faq.question: What is Katong-style laksa?
faq.answer: A Nyonya laksa from Katong with rich coconut gravy, vermicelli cut short for spoon-only eating, and toppings like cockles, prawns, fish cake, and bean sprouts.

faq.question: Where is the famous Katong laksa area?
faq.answer: Along East Coast Road between Joo Chiat and Marine Parade. Janggut, 328 Katong, and George's are all within a 10-minute walk. Take MRT to Paya Lebar.

faq.question: Is 328 Katong Laksa worth it?
faq.answer: It beat Gordon Ramsay in 2013. But locals debate quality vs price ($7.30+). Worth one visit; many prefer Janggut or Sungei Road for better value.

faq.question: What is the difference between Singapore laksa and Penang laksa?
faq.answer: Singapore laksa has creamy coconut broth. Penang laksa has sour tamarind fish broth with no coconut. Essentially different dishes.

faq.question: When is the best time to eat laksa?
faq.answer: Most stalls operate 8:30 AM to 3 PM. Arrive by 10-11 AM. 328 Katong is open until 9:30 PM.

methodology: We analyzed hundreds of Reddit posts and thousands of comments across relevant subreddits spanning 2019 to 2026. Places were ranked by frequency of independent recommendations and verified with Google ratings. Every spot was mentioned in at least 2 separate threads by different users.
